contribution: Development of structural empirical methods for analyzing demand, market power, and competition in differentiated-product industries (empirical industrial organization)
rationale: The 2025 prize went to macro/growth (Mokyr, Aghion, Howitt), so the committee may turn to applied microeconomics. The BLP framework, together with Pakes's work on dynamic oligopoly and productivity estimation, is foundational. It is used everywhere in antitrust, merger review and trade, and has long been a leading candidate. Main alternatives are New Keynesian monetary economics (Woodford, Galí, Blanchard) and public finance (Saez).
